set.body:
Problem:
Sojourn core currently imports scala-slurm-core contracts, while generic Sojourn storage and spool code import AtomicFiles from scala-slurm-worker. This is scheduler-neutral in meaning but not in package ownership or independent evolution.

Scope:
- Inventory every cross-repository type and primitive currently consumed by Sojourn.
- Introduce one neutral artifact or repository for the genuinely shared vocabulary: validated identifiers, content/schema codecs, diagnostics and evidence, freshness, retry provenance and epochs, and the atomic-file primitives used outside worker execution.
- Move AtomicFiles out of scala-slurm-worker without moving spool, queue, lease, scheduler, or worker policy into the neutral kernel.
- Migrate scala-slurm and Sojourn to the neutral ownership and remove obsolete aliases once migration is complete.
- Record an ADR naming the stable ownership rule and compatibility policy.

Acceptance criteria:
- sojourn-core has no dependency on scala-slurm-core, protocol, worker, managed, local, SSH, or agent artifacts.
- sojourn-runtime does not import AtomicFiles from a worker package.
- scala-slurm and Sojourn both depend downward on the neutral kernel; the kernel depends on neither repository runtime and no dependency cycle exists.
- Public packages and Scaladoc do not falsely present provider-neutral contracts as Slurm-owned.
- Atomic writes retain CREATE_NEW/private-temp/fsync/atomic-move/no-copy-fallback semantics and typed failures.
- Focused tests cover identifier validation, codec round trips and bounds, retry provenance preservation, digest identity, atomic claim races, symlink refusal, collision, replacement, and unsupported atomic move.
- Existing wire golden fixtures remain byte-identical unless a versioned migration with explicit compatibility tests is approved.
- Both repositories compile and test against the same locally published kernel version; dependency eviction reports are clean.
- The existing P6f.15 filesystem-sharing item is closed with evidence or explicitly superseded by this item, with no duplicated active scope.
set.title: SCOMP.1: Extract the scheduler-neutral shared kernel
